The key rule is: **the searchable database is rebuilt from the latest captured version of every retained declaration. Aliases are not an accumulated history of every name ever published.**

**1. A new version of an existing declaration**

The source decoder chooses the version with the latest publication date, breaking ties by register ID. Sync replaces the captured record with that declaration ID; its previous payments do not remain as additional current payments. The complete source JSON is retained as evidence, including any older versions supplied by the API, but only the selected version supplies funding observations. [Source decoder](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-delta/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_source.rs:179), [record replacement](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-delta/exposed/src/lib/domain/services/declaration_sync.rs:336).

For example, declaration 100 initially names **“Acme Ltd”**, company number **12345678**. Its replacement names **“Acme Holdings Ltd”**, with the same number:

- It resolves to the same company identity and keeps the same database funder ID.
- Its aliases are recalculated from current declarations.
- **“Acme Ltd” remains searchable if another current declaration still records that name for this identity.**
- If that name exists only in superseded versions, it disappears from searchable aliases. Its presence in raw evidence does not preserve it as an alias.

**2. A brand-new declaration**

Sync adds its ID to the retained declarations. Any changed capture triggers cleaning and resolution across the **whole retained corpus**, so the new evidence can change existing funder assignments too.

A new declaration naming **“Acme Trading Ltd”**, company number **12345678**, joins the same company identity and contributes that recorded name as an alias. A similar name without that company number is subject to the resolution rules; fuzzy similarity does not guarantee a merge. Company identities use the company number, while unanchored identities include the ingestion run ID. Consequently, **unanchored funders receive new database IDs on each changed full resolution**, even when their apparent grouping stays unchanged. [Identity construction](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-delta/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/identity.rs:444).

For both cases, the canonical display name is the most frequent recorded name in the resolved identity—not necessarily the newest name. Aliases come from its current recorded names. Only identities selected for at least one payment are loaded, though their other observations can contribute names. [Name and alias construction](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-delta/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs:402).

The loader replaces aliases and payments, removes funders left without payments, and rebuilds search/display grouping. That grouping can combine separate persisted funders, so a grouped search result need not mean resolution merged their identities. [Database replacement](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-delta/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs:643).
